frequency_question: What proportion of major federal agency rules complete the full notice-and-comment lifecycle and achieve final publication in the Federal Register within 362 days of initiating the formal proposal stage?
membership_rule: Includes rules classified as 'economically significant' or major under the Administrative Procedure Act that completed proposed and final stages; excludes interim final rules, direct final rules, and emergency declarations.

cases.name: EPA Mercury and Air Toxics Reconsideration (2019)

coverage_note: 5 named cases representing major regulatory actions across multiple departments; estimated historical completion rate for initiated major rules within 362 days is approximately 70-80% under cooperative conditions.
known_gaps: Excludes rules that experienced extended inter-agency delays or deep bureaucratic holdups prior to publication.
skeleton: Decomposition of federal rulemaking timelines by statutory minimum periods: Proposed Rule drafting (60 days) + OIRA Review (90 days) + Public Comment Period (60 days) + Final Rule Drafting & OIRA Final Review (120 days) = 330 minimum baseline days, leaving a 32-day buffer within the 362-day limit.
multiplier: Standard sequential administrative phases (4 distinct mandatory gates) each averaging 60-90 days, yielding a median total duration of 340 days for rules that successfully complete the process without stalling.
validity_reason: Administrative procedures and statutory review timeframes under the APA remain legally stable unless major statutory reforms occur.
